text:
ana: heads-up — planning a config-only rollout for routing/batching/timeouts on the inference fleet. target window: tonight 11pm-1am PT. change is traffic-only (no model binary). will pin fallback model variant for safety. asking for :eyes: and any objections by +2h.

sam: 👍 ok for me. what % canary do you want? region split?

ana: thinking 3% global for first 10m, then 10% for 20m, then 100% if no regressions. split across us-west/us-east only for initial canary. keep eu/apac off for now.

deploy-bot: build-checks OK. canary policy ready. to proceed run: `/deploy config --env prod --tag routing-batch-timeout-v1 --strategy canary` (dry-run available with `--dry`).

jia: quick note — the routing change reduces late-retry TTL from 500ms -> 200ms and tightens batch window to 8ms. worried about tail SLO on long context chats. can we pin a slower-but-stable variant (model-v1-p99) as fallback for 503/timeout errors?

ana: yes — plan includes explicit fallback to model-v1-p99 and route fallback to warm pool. will include a soft rate floor so we don't throttle paid customers.

will: ran a dry-run earlier on staging for 6h. p50 improved, p99 up ~8% for the largest sequences. I pushed a short log snippet to the release doc: `staging/2026-03-18/routing-batch-v1.log` — no error spike but observed a slight increase in memory evictions on a subset of hosts.

ana: thanks will. action item: ops to increase warm_pool_min by +1 for canary nodes. ops, please ack.

sam: ops acked in infra ticket #INFR-4123. I'll also add an automated smoke test that hits long-context endpoints every minute during canary.

deploy-bot: deploy initiated at 3819991150. canary 3% (us-west/us-east). monitors: latency-p50, latency-p99, error-rate, model-fallback-rate, mem-evict-rate.

deploy-bot: canary pass @ +12m: p50 ok, p99 borderline +6%, error-rate normal, mem-evict-rate slight uptick (1.4x baseline). continuing to 10%.

jia: borderline p99 — do we have immediate rollback criteria? propose: rollback if p99 >= +10% OR error-rate >= 2x OR model-fallback-rate > 0.5% sustained 5m.

ana: agreed. i'm going to hold at 10% for 20m and watch the smoke tests + warm pool behavior.

deploy-bot: ramp to 10% at 3819991180.

will: smoke tests show 1 failure out of 120 in the first 10m — a 503 on a long prompt, fallback triggered successfully. logging indicates timeouts at 210ms threshold.

ana: because fallback worked, i'm inclined to proceed to 50% but tighten the timeout back to 250ms for the next tranche to reduce tail failures. propose: batch_window=8ms, request_timeout=250ms, retry_ttl=250ms.

sam: fine with that conservative tweak. put it in the config and redeploy as config-only patch (no model swap).

deploy-bot: paused original canary. new config candidate pushed as `routing-batch-timeout-v1a`.

ana: rolling the patched config to 10% first then 50% if looks good. ops: please keep warm pool bumped.

deploy-bot: canary resumed at 3819991195 with v1a at 10%.

deploy-bot: monitor update @ +8m: p99 back down to +3%, error-rate stable, fallback-rate ~0.2%. mem-evict-rate unchanged.

ana: looks safe. proceeding to 50% over next 10m. will notify product and support.

deploy-bot: ramp to 50% at 3819991210.

sam: adding a release note: "Config-only: routing/batching/timeouts. Added model fallback to model-v1-p99, warm_pool_min +1 for canary, conservative request timeout 250ms. Canary staged US regions first." filing in release notes doc link: http://go/release-notes/RI-2026-03-config

ana: final check — no objections, moving to full rollout tomorrow 2am PT if overnight metrics steady. :tada:

deploy-bot: deploy snapshot: `{ "tag": "routing-batch-timeout-v1a", "status": "partial", "percent": "50", "start_ts": "3819991150" }`
